Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02 14:00 UTC

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): ok everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, uh, we'll run about 45 to 60 minutes, just to align the renewal and the regional sprint.
[00:14] Rachel (Bridgehaven): thanks, Maya. we've got Priya and Omar on because security's key for the Japan plan and compliance. we also want to nail the cost math.
[00:28] Maya: great, quick round robin — what changed since last checkin? Omar?
[00:33] Omar: yeah so traffic's up about 30% month over month on our recommendation API; peak seq length hasn't changed but qps spike windows are larger. we need predictable per-token cost for bursts.
[00:45] Liam (Redwood SE): got it. that matches what we saw on the sample traces — the prefix reuse is pretty high so caching will help. We can show cost delta with and without KV cache for your exact shape.
[01:02] Priya: two security gates: one is KMS/HSM for keys and the other is audit log retention to satisfy our third party comp attestations. SOC2 is table stakes.
[01:18] Devika (CSM): quick note — Bridgehaven's current renewal is end of month so we want to make progress this week to avoid service disruption.
[01:26] Rachel: mmhmm — can you summarize options? dedicated, hosted, private?
[01:33] Maya: yes. Option A: 12mo renewal, stay hosted for majority, add Japan region as hosted (fastest). Option B: 12/24mo with Dedicated reserved capacity for steady qps and a VPC/private deployment for PII workflows (we call it private plane in our docs sometimes, sorry — private control plane). Option C: hybrid — Dedicated baseline + hosted burst and Japan as dedicated when you need low latency.
[02:05] Ethan: how different are latencies across eu vs apac regions? checkout is sensitive — we need sub-200ms to hoist conversion.
[02:15] Liam: realistic numbers: in-hosted eu region 120–160ms median for a 512 token request; apac (Japan) hosted tends to be 160–240ms depending on peering. Dedicated in-region reduces that by about 20–40ms on average; also collocating model variants and kernel selection reduces jitter.
[02:44] Omar: ok and cost tradeoffs?
[02:48] Maya: with Dedicated you buy reserved GPU capacity so unit cost per token drops, predictability goes up, but commit is required. We gave you the commitment ladder in the spreadsheet; I'll update that for Japan pricing.
[03:02] Priya: on the private/VPC piece — do you integrate with customer KMS? we need bring-your-own-key.
[03:09] Liam: yes, BYOK via KMS is supported. small note: on-prem package has additional setup time and some ops handoff. We have a KMS runbook. I'll share, but please flag any special HSM vendors you use.
[03:30] Priya: we use Azure Key Vault for most keys, but for a small set we do HSM via Thales.
[03:36] Liam: fine, we have customers on Thales; we'll include that in the scope.
[03:42] Rachel: what about audit logs and retention? our compliance team wants 2 years of immutable logs.
[03:49] Devika: Redwood Console supports export and retention tiers; longer retention is an add-on. We can include export to S3 for long-term immutable retention.
[04:00] Ethan: pilot — we need to run a real-world throughput test. what do you need from us?
[04:07] Liam: sample traffic, auth token for test env, and a short runbook. For throughput we'll spin up a dedicated job in our staging, run two 6-hour windows across typical and peak traffic shapes. We'll also exercise fallback policies and canary rollouts.
[04:26] Omar: we'll provide traffic csv and some synthetic burst curves.
[04:30] Maya: timeline — pilot this Thu–Fri? ok that might be tight though. what's realistic?
[04:36] Liam: realistically, we need 48–72 hours to provision a dedicated mini-pool in staging and run the first pass. so early next week is safer unless you can pre-provision.
[04:48] Rachel: next week is ok. can you scope how long Japan onboarding takes?
[04:53] Maya: hosted Japan adds within ~48 hours after contract (region enablement), Dedicated in-region can take 5–10 business days depending on capacity and infra scheduling. On-prem is longer — usually 4–8 weeks.
[05:08] Priya: any change to data residency? we need to ensure PII never leaves Japan for that workflow.
[05:15] Liam: for that we recommend Private deployment in the Japan region or a VPC endpoint with strict routing. We'll also configure per-route routing policies to keep certain endpoints in-region.
[05:29] Omar: what's the fallback if a region has a short outage — can requests reroute to eu? what's the SLA impact?
[05:36] Liam: yes, automated fallback is possible but you'll see higher latency if routed cross-region; we can set policy to failover to warm Dedicated in another region with an increased cost. We can also have a degraded mode.
[05:50] Rachel: okay, commercial — our CFO wants to avoid a big up-front. is there a mid-ground?
[05:57] Maya: yes — shorter commit term or a tiered commit with burst credits. We can model a 12mo with optional 3mo renew extension to lower near-term cost. I'll update the numbers.
[06:10] Ethan: competitors — we had a bench vs AICoreVault and CloudPrompt; their pricing looked lower for raw hosted but lacked VPC integrations and audit tooling we need.
[06:24] Priya: exactly — security is a gating factor.
[06:27] Maya: noted. next steps: I'll share an updated quote that includes Japan region hosted price, and a Dedicated pricing option with a 3-month burst band. Liam will prep the pilot runbook and benchmark checklist including KV-cache enabled/disabled. Priya will send the compliance doc. Omar will send traffic sample.
[06:45] Rachel: sounds good. can we set an internal decision target by next Thursday?
[06:50] Devika: yes — I'll put a go/no-go checkpoint in calendar for 2026-05-13.
[06:56] Maya: ok wrapping — I'll drop the quote and a 1-pager on region timelines.
[07:02] Liam: and I'll shoot the runbook link and a quick spreadsheet with expected latency/cost deltas.
[07:09] Priya: thanks, we'll review and get compliance notes back.
[07:13] Rachel: thank you all.
